method: Verbatim excerpt. Attached only when the sentence names this player unambiguously and names no other board player. Surnames shared by two board players (Brown) require the full name.

notes.A.J. Brown: A.J. Brown's 2025 felt underwhelming, but he still finished 12th among WRs in PPR points per game and 17th in yards per route.
notes.Christian McCaffrey: If those top four guys are off the board, you'll find McCaffrey topping the rankings in your Draft War Room.
notes.Christian Watson: Watson ranked 19th among WRs in PPR points per game last year, registering career bests in yards per route and PFF receiving grade, despite coming off a January 2025 ACL tear.
notes.Colston Loveland: Loveland proved efficient throughout his rookie season and closed strong.
notes.Davante Adams: Adams is in for some regression after scoring 14 times in 14 games last year. But he’ll once again be one of the best TD bets at the position. He ranked top 3 among WRs in red-zone targets, targets inside the 10, and end-zone targets last year.
notes.Drake London: London ranked eighth among WRs in both expected and actual PPR points per game last year. He drew a 29.2% target share and has now topped 28% in three of four NFL seasons.
notes.Drake Maye: Maye was spectacular last year, leading the league in both completion rate and yards per attempt. He finished third among QBs in fantasy points per game.
notes.George Kittle: Kittle's Achilles injury obviously adds risk, but a 9th-round cost makes him relatively replaceable if it doesn't work out. The upside is just as obvious: Kittle remained one of the most efficient TEs in the league last year, finishing third at his position in PPR points per game.
notes.J.K. Dobbins: Dobbins was Denver's clear lead back ahead of R.J. Harvey before last year's season-ending injury. He averaged 15.3 carries and ranked 23rd among RBs in PPR points per game through Week 10.
notes.Jacory Croskey-Merritt: Croskey-Merritt ran well as a rookie last year, averaging 4.6 yards per carry and ranking top 12 among 51 qualifying RBs in rush yards over expected per carry and yards after contact per carry.
notes.Jahmyr Gibbs: Gibbs saw an increased role over the second half of last season, averaging 14.4 carries and 7.0 targets per game. He led all RBs with 24.8 PPR points per game over that stretch.
notes.Kyler Murray: Murray beat out J.J. McCarthy for Minnesota's starting job and boasts obvious top-12 upside thanks to his rushing ability, HC Kevin O’Connell’s scheme, and the Vikings’ weaponry.
notes.Malik Nabers: Nabers seemingly has a good chance to be ready come Week 1 and could be a league-winner from Round 3. He finished WR7 in PPR points per game as a rookie and was sitting ninth through Week 3 last year, before the knee injury.
notes.Michael Pittman: Pittman has been a strong target earner, posting a 20+% target share in five straight seasons. He has a good chance to make it six straight this year in Pittsburgh, where the Steelers have very little proven production beyond D.K. Metcalf.
notes.Rashee Rice: It's been a tumultuous offseason for Rice, but he's on track to be out there for Week 1. A healthy Rice has been a fantasy monster, averaging 18.3 PPR points over his last 21 games. Only five WRs (including Rice himself) averaged more last year.
notes.Rashid Shaheed: Shaheed is a classic post-hype sleeper. He struggled after last year's midseason trade to Seattle. But a full offseason to settle into the offense should mean a much more productive 2026.
notes.Sam LaPorta: The back injury that ended LaPorta’s 2025 season adds risk but also delivers a deep discount. This guy was a fifth- or sixth-round pick in most drafts last year. LaPorta was producing just fine before going down last season, ranking seventh among TEs in PPR points per game.
notes.Saquon Barkley: Barkley disappointed last year, finishing 15th among RBs in PPR points per game. He still ranked seventh at the position in expected points, though, and was generally held back by a sagging Eagles offense. There’s bounce-back potential for the unit in 2026 under new OC Sean Mannion.
notes.Stefon Diggs: Diggs remained very effective on a per-route basis last year, ranking 15th in targets per route and seventh in yards per route among 76 qualifying WRs.
notes.Tyjae Spears: Spears has established himself as a productive pass-catching back, ranking 13th at his position in total receptions and 14th in receiving yards over the last three seasons. That gives him a nice base in PPR leagues.

source: Draft Sharks, "Fantasy Football Draft Guide: 12-Team PPR Draft Strategy"
